planes.name: DC-3
planes.blurb: 1936 carbon-mic interphone into a weak horn speaker. Lots of grain, almost no level, dropouts in the wiring.

dossier.system: Carbon-mic interphone into a later horn speaker
dossier.good: You can tell a human is talking. That is about it.
dossier.bad: Almost no level against the radials. Extreme grain, horn-narrow band, wiring dropouts up to half a second. Loudspeakers were barely practical in that noise.
dossier.more: WWII-era ships used headphones first. A cabin PA on a DC-3 is a retrofit: pencil-tube or carbon chain, one weak horn, no automatic gain, no zone amps.

planes.blurb: Early jet analog amp. Nasal, narrow, and a little shaky on long runs.

dossier.good: Speech is intelligible in the midrange if the crew leans in.
dossier.bad: Nasal, narrow, amp sag on long reads. Cabin noise eats the edges. Skips show up on tired wiring.
dossier.more: First-generation jet PA. Designed only to beat 70–80 dB cruise roar, not to sound like a room.

planes.blurb: Trijet analog PA. Mid honk, limited top end, occasional amplifier sag.

dossier.good: A bit more mid punch than a 707. Crew can cut through the aft engines.
dossier.bad: Honky mids, chopped top end, occasional amplifier sag. Still analog and fussy.
dossier.more: Same design brief as other 1960s Boeings: one amp, many cheap speakers, intelligibility over fidelity.

planes.blurb: JT8D-era 5-inch speakers. Harsh and telephone-like.

dossier.good: Close seats, so level is usually enough.
dossier.bad: Harsh, telephone-like, peaky around 2 kHz. Sounds like someone talking through a tin can.
dossier.more: Classic 737 PA amp on the battery bus. Gain steps up when engines run. The speakers never got better than speech-band cones.

planes.blurb: Classic 737 analog PA. Cleaner than the -200, still band-limited.

dossier.system: Improved analog PA, same small cones
dossier.good: Cleaner than the -200. Less grit, more consistent gain.
dossier.bad: Still band-limited. No per-speaker DSP. A little boxy.
dossier.more: Classic-era amp cleanup, not a new architecture. You hear a 737, just a tidier one.

planes.blurb: NG PA amp, about 5-inch 7 W PSU speakers. Gain steps up with engines; still speech-band.

dossier.system: NG PA amp + REU, 5-inch 7 W PSU speakers
dossier.good: Predictable level. Engine-on +6 dB gain. Most people understand it.
dossier.bad: Still a speech-band cone in the PSU. Nasal Boeing mid honk. Overhead bins create small dead spots.
dossier.more: The default modern 737 sound. Pilot priority, then attendants, then recorded PA. Not hi-fi on purpose.

planes.name: 737 MAX 8
planes.blurb: Same small speakers, newer processing. A bit cleaner, still not hi-fi.

dossier.good: A bit cleaner and less shouty than NG. Fewer dropouts.
dossier.bad: Same small cones. You cannot process your way out of a 3–4 inch driver.
dossier.more: Electronics moved on; the cabin speaker did not. Sounds like a 737 that had a software update.

planes.blurb: Analog jumbo. Long cabin, more slap, more dead spots under the bins.

dossier.good: You hear it in the mid cabin if you sit under a speaker.
dossier.bad: Long tube, lots of slap, bins kill 2 kHz. Dead spots and dropouts are common. Grainy analog chain.
dossier.more: Widebody coverage is the hard problem. Early 747s used conventional cones with uneven SPL row to row.

planes.blurb: Later 747 amp, still a long tube of ceiling speakers.

dossier.good: More even than a -200. Better amp, still understandable aft.
dossier.bad: The cabin is still a hallway of speakers. Echo and bin shadows remain.
dossier.more: Same layout problem, better electronics. Intelligibility improved; hi-fi did not arrive.

planes.blurb: Modern jumbo electronics, huge cabin. Cleaner chain, more room sound.

dossier.good: Clean chain. Speech is clear when you are near a speaker.
dossier.bad: The room is enormous. You get hall-like slap and some coverage gaps.
dossier.more: Best 747 electronics, worst 747 geometry. The mix is clean and a little cathedral.

planes.blurb: Loud, a little piercing. Narrow-body Boeing mid honk.

dossier.good: Loud. Cuts cruise noise. People in the back hear it.
dossier.bad: Piercing mid honk. Can sound shouty. Not warm.
dossier.more: The 757 PA is famous for being present, not pretty. A long single-aisle with a hot 2 kHz bump.

planes.blurb: 1980s widebody analog/digital hybrid. Boxy, some aisle fade.

dossier.good: Fuller than a 737. Twin-aisle has more speaker options.
dossier.bad: Boxy 80s voicing. Aisle fade and bin shadows. Some skip risk.
dossier.more: First-gen widebody Boeing PA. Designed around STI, not music. Uneven at the window seats.

planes.blurb: Early digital widebody. Fuller than a 737, still PSU cones.

dossier.good: Fuller and cleaner than 80s Boeings. Fewer analog artifacts.
dossier.bad: Still cone speakers. A little echo. Not 787-quiet.
dossier.more: First Boeing that feels like a modern system. Speech-band by choice, digital by architecture.

planes.name: 777-300ER
planes.blurb: Longer 777 cabin. Same digital chain, a bit more echo aft.

dossier.good: Same clean digital feed as the -200.
dossier.bad: More echo aft. Tail speakers are a long way from the handset.
dossier.more: Stretch the cabin and the PA stays the same. You hear distance more than you hear new hardware.

planes.blurb: DSP PA in a quieter composite cabin. Cleaner and less shouty.

dossier.system: DSP PA, IFE override, modern CIDS-class director
dossier.good: Quiet cabin means less shouting. Cleaner band, less grain, rare skips.
dossier.bad: Still not a studio. Small speakers, some cabin slap.
dossier.more: Best Boeing here. DSP, lower ambient, headphone PA ducking on some airlines. The mix can stay quieter and still read.

planes.blurb: Same 787 system, slightly longer cabin.

dossier.good: Same clean 787 chain.
dossier.bad: A slightly longer room. A bit more tail delay.
dossier.more: Same directors and speakers as the -8. You are hearing cabin length, not a different radio.

planes.name: 797 (NMA)
planes.blurb: Unbuilt NMA. Great flight-deck mic, quiet composite cabin, DSP PA that actually sounds like a person.

dossier.system: Clean-sheet DSP PA, 787-class cabin, great flight-deck mic
dossier.good: The mic is the point. Close, quiet, little boom. Composite cabin is hush. Wide band, almost no grain, almost no skips. It sounds like a person, not a telephone.
dossier.bad: It was never built. This is the NMA as promised: 787 tech in a smaller room. Your airline does not have one.
dossier.more: Boeing’s New Midsize Airplane, often called 797. 225-seat NMA-6X and 275-seat NMA-7X studies, composite airframe, high-bypass engines, 787-family systems. Shelved after the MAX crisis and A321XLR. In this sim it is the great-mic plane: boom-rejecting handset, quiet cruise, DSP that does not have to shout.

planes.name: 747SP
planes.blurb: Short jumbo. Analog 747 PA in a stubbier tube. Still grainy, less hallway than a -200.

dossier.system: Analog 747 PA in a stubbier tube
dossier.good: Shorter than a -200, so less hallway. Still a real jumbo speaker count.
dossier.bad: Same analog grain and bin shadows. Special-performance does not mean special PA.
dossier.more: 747SP cut the fuselage for range. The PA amp family is 1970s jumbo. You hear a shorter 747, not a new radio.

planes.blurb: MD-95 in Boeing paint. Rear-engine regional, a bit nasal, short-cabin analog.

dossier.system: Late MD analog PA, short cabin
dossier.good: Short cabin, enough level, less echo than an MD-80 stretch.
dossier.bad: Still nasal. Rear engines and a Douglas-family cone.
dossier.more: Boeing inherited the MD-95. It is a tidy regional, not a 787. The PA never got a clean-sheet.

planes.blurb: 777X. New digital cabin, long folding-wing widebody. Clean chain, still a long room.

dossier.good: Modern directors, wide band, low grain. Cleaner than a 777-300ER.
dossier.bad: Very long room. Tail delay and a little bloom remain.
dossier.more: 777X cabin systems are new; the fuselage is still a long twin-aisle. Electronics improved, geometry did not shrink.

planes.name: VC-25A
planes.blurb: Air Force One 747-200. Special comms and redundant amps. Cabin PA is better than a stock jumbo.

dossier.system: Redundant special-mission comms plus cabin PA
dossier.good: Better amps, backups, and a treated cabin. Crew can be understood.
dossier.bad: Still a 747-200 room. Some slap. Not a 797 mic.
dossier.more: VC-25A is Air Force One’s 747-200. The comms suite is special-mission. The passenger-address path is a stock jumbo that got extra care and redundancy, not a studio.

planes.name: 747 LCF
planes.blurb: Dreamlifter. Cargo bulge, almost no passenger cabin. PA is a warehouse horn.

dossier.system: Cargo-hold PA / horn in a bubble
dossier.good: Someone on the cargo floor can hear a shout.
dossier.bad: No real passenger cabin. Huge volume, slap, grain. Warehouse acoustics.
dossier.more: Dreamlifter. The upper lobe is for 787 barrels. A PA here is a safety horn, not a cabin announcement.

planes.name: A220-300
planes.blurb: Small CSeries cabin, relatively even coverage for a regional jet.

dossier.good: Short cabin, even rows, relatively clean. Easy to understand.
dossier.bad: Still a regional cone. A little thin on the bottom.
dossier.more: Bombardier-era acoustics. Small room is an advantage. One of the least painful modern PAs.

planes.name: A300-600
planes.blurb: Early widebody Airbus. Analog character, uneven rows.

dossier.good: Widebody speakers can get loud enough.
dossier.bad: Grainy, uneven rows, analog leftovers. Skips are common.
dossier.more: Before the mature CIDS director era. Sounds older than an A320 even when the airframe is similar vintage.

planes.name: A310
planes.blurb: Shorter A300 cousin. Same generation PA, still grainy.

dossier.good: Shorter cabin than the A300, so a bit less echo.
dossier.bad: Same grainy chain. Still analog in the bones.
dossier.more: Same generation, slightly less hallway. Not a new system.

planes.name: A318
planes.blurb: Short CIDS cabin. A little boxy, not much echo.

dossier.system: CIDS, per-speaker amps, six audio channels
dossier.good: Short cabin, consistent CIDS levels, little echo.
dossier.bad: Boxy small-cone voicing. Digital, not warm.
dossier.more: CIDS is the Airbus idea: director, DEU-A, programmed gain/EQ per speaker. The baby bus shows that at its most even.

planes.name: A319
planes.blurb: A320-family CIDS. Digital, consistent, still small PSU cones.

dossier.good: Even coverage. Less row fade than an A321.
dossier.bad: Small PSU cones. Speech-band EQ on purpose.
dossier.more: Same CIDS as the A320. The shorter tube is the upgrade.

planes.name: A320
planes.blurb: Classic CIDS: digital feed, per-speaker amps, speech-band EQ.

dossier.system: CIDS: digital director, DEU-A, per-speaker amps
dossier.good: Consistent zones. Programmable EQ. Digital feed is cleaner than old Boeing analog.
dossier.bad: Still 3–4 inch cones. A little hollow. Not hi-fi.
dossier.more: The textbook Airbus PA. Three attendant channels, three passenger channels, speaker-by-speaker gain. Built for STI, not music.

planes.name: A321
planes.blurb: Same CIDS as the A320, longer tube, more row-to-row fade.

dossier.good: Same digital consistency up front.
dossier.bad: More row-to-row fade and a little slap in the back.
dossier.more: Identical directors, more seats. The PA does not grow with the fuselage.

planes.name: A330-200
planes.blurb: Widebody CIDS. Warmer than a Boeing 767, some cabin slap.

dossier.good: Warmer and fuller than a 767. Digital zones.
dossier.bad: Cabin slap. Window seats still sit in bin shadows.
dossier.more: CIDS scaled to a twin-aisle. Better electronics than early Boeings; the room still wins some arguments.

planes.name: A330-300
planes.blurb: Longer A330. Same directors, more distance to the tail speakers.

dossier.good: Same A330 voicing.
dossier.bad: More distance to the tail. A bit more echo.
dossier.more: Stretch penalty. Hardware is the same; the last rows hear more hallway.

planes.name: A340-300
planes.blurb: Older four-engine widebody. A bit hollow, more analog leftovers.

dossier.good: Understandable, a little warmer than a 747-200.
dossier.bad: Hollow, grainier than later A330s. More skip risk.
dossier.more: Same family as the A330, earlier production feel. The PA sounds a generation behind a late A330.

planes.name: A340-600
planes.blurb: Very long cabin. Coverage gaps and a trailing echo are common.

dossier.system: Older CIDS in a huge tube
dossier.good: It reaches the back, usually.
dossier.bad: Coverage gaps, trailing echo, hollow mids. One of the harder Airbuses to make even.
dossier.more: Longest single-deck Airbus of its day. Electronics cannot hide a 75-meter hallway.

planes.name: A350-900
planes.blurb: Modern DSP CIDS in a quiet cabin. Clearest Airbus here.

dossier.good: Clearest Airbus here. Wide band, low grain, rare skips, quiet cabin.
dossier.bad: Still a PA. A little cabin bloom, not a close mic.
dossier.more: This is what CIDS looks like after DSP and a quieter airframe. Speech can stay natural and still beat cruise noise.

planes.name: A350-1000
planes.blurb: Same A350 chain, longer cabin.

dossier.good: Same clean A350 chain.
dossier.bad: Slightly more tail delay than the -900.
dossier.more: Same directors. You are hearing length, not a different radio.

planes.name: A380-800
planes.blurb: Two decks, long paths. Clean electronics, the most hall-like cabin.

dossier.good: Clean electronics. Lots of speakers. Zones can be balanced.
dossier.bad: Most hall-like cabin. Long paths, deck-to-deck differences, some coverage holes.
dossier.more: Best example of 'the system is good and the room is the problem.' Two decks, long lines, lots of slap.

planes.name: A320neo
planes.blurb: Same CIDS bones as the A320, quieter LEAP/PW engines. A little cleaner than ceo.

dossier.good: Same even CIDS as ceo, a bit less engine roar to fight.
dossier.bad: Same small cones. Not a new PA architecture.
dossier.more: neo changed the engines. The director and DEU-A are still A320 family. Cleaner only because the room is quieter.

planes.name: A321XLR
planes.blurb: Long-range single-aisle. CIDS is fine; the extra tanks and length add a bit of fade aft.

dossier.good: Digital, consistent up front. Fine for a single-aisle.
dossier.bad: Longest A321. More fade and slap in the last rows.
dossier.more: The XLR is an A321 with range. CIDS did not grow. Rear tanks and length are the PA story.

planes.name: Beluga XL
planes.blurb: A330-743L outsize cargo. The upper lobe is a hangar. PA is a cargo-hold shout.

dossier.system: A330 CIDS leftover in a cargo lobe
dossier.good: You can page the cargo deck.
dossier.bad: The upper lobe is a hangar. Echo, hollow mids, no passenger trim.
dossier.more: Beluga XL moves A350 wings. There is almost no airline cabin. The PA is industrial.

planes.name: Concorde
planes.blurb: Mach 2 narrow cabin, 1960s analog. Tiny, loud, and very nasal over the intakes.

dossier.good: Short cabin, so you are never far from a speaker.
dossier.bad: Intake and skin noise, nasal analog, dropouts. A glamorous telephone.
dossier.more: Concorde’s cabin is small and loud. The PA is contemporary with early widebodies, not with the speed. Intelligibility over the intakes was the whole design.

planes.name: L-1011 TriStar
planes.blurb: Autoland-era widebody. Smoother analog than a DC-10. Still 1970s cones.

dossier.good: Smoother than a DC-10. Lockheed spent on systems. Speech is even.
dossier.bad: Still cones and analog grain. Widebody slap.
dossier.more: The TriStar was the over-engineered one. Autoland and a nicer cabin, but the PA is still 1972. Better manners, same physics.

planes.name: DC-10
planes.blurb: Trijet widebody analog. Honky, grainy, and a little harsh in the back.

dossier.good: Loud enough in the mid cabin.
dossier.bad: Harsh, grainy, honky. Aft is a long way from the handset.
dossier.more: DC-10 PA is the blunt instrument next to the L-1011. Same era, less polish.

planes.name: MD-80
planes.blurb: Rear-engine Mad Dog. Famous nasal PA. Sounds like a drive-through speaker.

dossier.good: You will hear it. The 2 kHz bump cuts the cabin.
dossier.bad: Famous nasal ‘Mad Dog’ PA. Drive-through energy. Grain and skips.
dossier.more: MD-80 announcements are a genre. Rear engines, a long thin tube, and a honky analog amp. People remember the sound.

planes.name: MD-11
planes.blurb: Stretched DC-10 family. A bit cleaner, still analog, long-cabin slap.

dossier.good: A step up from the DC-10. A bit fuller.
dossier.bad: Long cabin, leftover honk, slap in the back.
dossier.more: MD-11 is a DC-10 that went to finishing school. The PA improved. The hallway got longer.

planes.name: BAe 146
planes.blurb: Whisper jet outside, cheap regional PA inside. Short cabin, boxy cones.

dossier.good: Short cabin. Whisper engines outside help a little.
dossier.bad: Boxy, thin, budget cones. Not a 146 luxury inside.
dossier.more: Quiet approach, ordinary PA. The whisper is airframe and engines, not the speakers.

planes.name: Fokker 100
planes.blurb: Rear-engine regional. Tidy Dutch analog, still telephone-band.

dossier.good: Even enough. Less hysteria than an MD-80.
dossier.bad: Telephone band. A little nasal.
dossier.more: Fokker’s last airliner. Competent, not romantic. The PA matches: tidy and limited.

planes.name: Dash 8 Q400
planes.blurb: Loud turboprop. PA has to shout over the props. Harsh and close.

dossier.good: It is loud on purpose. You hear the crew over the blades.
dossier.bad: Harsh, close, shouty. Almost no low end. Fatigue.
dossier.more: Q400 cabins are prop-noise environments. The PA is a megaphone. Intelligibility is a volume fight.

planes.name: ATR 72-600
planes.blurb: High-wing turboprop. Same fight with prop noise. Thin, loud, a little scratchy.

dossier.system: Regional PA vs prop and gearbox
dossier.good: Short cabin, enough shout.
dossier.bad: Thin, scratchy, drowned at the window seats.
dossier.more: ATR 72-600 is newer than a Q400 in avionics, not in cabin hush. Same physics: props win, PA yells.

planes.name: E195-E2
planes.blurb: Modern E-Jet. Quiet for a regional, clean digital PA, even rows.

dossier.good: Even rows, clean band, low grain. Easy to understand.
dossier.bad: Still a regional cone. A little thin.
dossier.more: E2 is the grown-up E-Jet. Cabin noise dropped; the PA can stay polite. One of the better speciality regionals.

planes.name: C919
planes.blurb: New Chinese narrowbody. Honeywell-class cabin systems. Clean, a little generic.

dossier.good: Clean, consistent, modern. No analog honk.
dossier.bad: Generic. Small-cone speech band. Not a 797 mic.
dossier.more: C919 uses bought-in cabin electronics. It sounds like a new A320-class jet: fine, even, unmemorable.
